note: ISA facts per architecture, regenerated by `tools/bench/isa_probe/isa_probe.py regenerate` from the committed probe outputs in src/core/data/isa_probe/ (one isa_probe_<arch>.txt per architecture, written by `isa_probe.py run` on one card of it; never edited by hand). In SM clocks unless the unit says otherwise: tensor pipe cycles per MMA at the SM and per partition (and with one CTA of 4, 8, 16 warps on the SM) and the dependent MMA latency, all per PTX mma.sync of the row's mma_shape (on sm_70 one mma.sync.m8n8k4 is four SASS HMMA.884 STEPs, elsewhere one HMMA: the row's sass_per_mma, read from the build's SASS, from probe 17), INT32 / FP32 cycles per warp instruction (the FP32 figure with the loop's counter, compare and branch in it), the dependent latencies of the decode chains' ALU ops (lat_add_chain the add ptxas makes of a doubling, IADD3 and IMAD.IADD alternating up to sm_89; each conversion alone from probe 17), dependent L1 / L2 / DRAM load latencies alone and under 2, 4, 8 chasing warps per SM (the L2 and DRAM ones in wall ns too, with the SM clock of the chase; DRAM in a small range per warp, over the whole buffer, and with all 32 lanes of a warp chasing, on every SM and on half of them), shared-memory latency. The load latencies are given twice: on a chip that runs nothing else, and beside one warp of FFMAs on every SM (`_held`), where the SM clock is the working one (sm_clock_mhz_chase_held; sm_clock_mhz_mma under the tensor loop). The DRAM ns figures step with the ~1 us %globaltimer over 512 (one lane) or 256 (32 lanes) links: about 2 and 4 ns. Every row names its source file, the card, the probe version, nvcc, driver and runtime, and from probe 17 the sha256 of the isa_probe.cu it was built from, the build's -arch, the memory clock the card is rated at and, in its notes, the compute processes on its GPU before, during and after the run and the clocks nvidia-smi saw during it; provenance is Measured for all. A row is what its own probe version measured: up to probe 13 a link of the L1 / L2 / DRAM chains carried the chain's index-to-address ops beside the load, up to probe 16 the sm_70 shared link a shift beside the LDS. tests/test_isa_facts.py pins the schema, that the table equals its regeneration, and that every row comes from the checked-in probe source.
